thread:
laura: heads up — spotted anomalous access after last night's RBAC migration. reporting-sa made a SELECT against customer_redacted.sensitive_table at 02:14 UTC. looks like the affinity-mapper rule included a wildcard that matched the reporting service. can someone triage?

mike: pulling logs now. short snippet: `2026-03-20T02:14:12Z reporting-sa@prod SELECT FROM customer_redacted.sensitive_table`

opsbot: deploy:rbac-migration applied by @sanjay (commit 9f4b2a3). affected namespaces: analytics, reporting.

sanjay: that migration introduced the new role-affinity label matcher. I tested locally but must've missed the fallback case where label=="*" -> matches service accounts.

jen: ack. immediate containment options: 1) remove new RoleBinding in reporting namespace, 2) add explicit deny for reporting-sa on that resource, 3) revoke reporting-sa tokens / short-lived creds. which do we want now?

laura: prioritize expelling access first — remove the RoleBinding. then revoke creds. if rollback is fast we can do that.

mike: running `kubectl -n reporting delete rolebinding rb-affinity-mapper-9f4b2a3` now. pasted output: `rolebinding.rbac.authorization.k8s.io "rb-affinity-mapper-9f4b2a3" deleted`

jen: thanks. please also run `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=reporting-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and rotate keys if any are long-lived.

sanjay: confirmed deleted. I'm also preparing a small deny-policy to attach to the reporting namespace so accidental matches won't allow cross-tenant reads: `deny if resource == "customer_redacted.sensitive_table" && principal == "reporting-sa"` — will stage as a short-term guard.

opsbot: alert: 2 more SELECTs observed at 02:15 and 02:16. each returned limited rows; looks like analytics job pulled a subset.

laura: did any exfil look suspicious? size / destinations?

mike: outputs went to internal s3 bucket `prod-reporting-exports` (same project). bucket access is private. no external egress detected. still needs audit.

sec-guardian: flagging as P1 access-control regression. Create an incident and escalate to oncall infra-sec. Suggested impact: potential exposure of a small set of customer rows.

jen: oncall infra-sec pinged. I'll coordinate with infra to rotate CMK if needed. question: is the table encrypted with our KMS CMK or customer-managed?

mike: data at rest for that table is encrypted with CMK `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/data/cryptoKeys/cmk-prod-01`. reporting-sa had decryption rights via service account IAM binding? not normally. will verify IAM on key.

sanjay: quick check: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy cmk-prod-01 --keyring=data --location=global` -> shows a binding: `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` to group `analytics-engineers@redwood.com` and `serviceAccount:reporting-sa@...` (this is the problem). that binding predates the RBAC change, looks like a manual grant from onboarding script.

laura: ok two vectors: RBAC role + KMS binding. Containment: revoke reporting-sa from KMS policy immediately and rotate any keys used to decrypt recent exports. Jen, can you remove the SA from the key policy?

jen: doing `gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding cmk-prod-01 --member=serviceAccount:reporting-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` now. done.

mike: I also revoked active tokens for reporting-sa and issued a forced key rotation for any long-lived key material used by the reporting pipeline. posted PR to infra: `rotate-reporting-sa-keys` (link: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/482).

sanjay: rolling back the affinity-mapper change in the RBAC migration branch now. PR: https://git.redwood/platform/pulls/338 — includes test for wildcard label matching and explicit negative test.

laura: good. next: audit trail. we need a list of queries and rows accessed and an Affected Customers list. Mike, can you run a forensic query to enumerate rows returned during the time window and export to incident channel?

mike: running query against audit logs: `SELECT request, response_size, destination_bucket FROM audit_logs WHERE principal='reporting-sa' AND time >= '2026-03-20T02:10:00Z' AND time <= '2026-03-20T02:20:00Z'` — results show 3 selects, 154 rows total returned. exporting to secure incident artifact store now. link: (internal).

sec-guardian: also recommend enabling per-principal KMS audit logs and adding an alert for any service account that has both DB read and KMS decrypt permissions. This was the dangerous combo.

jen: yes — creating a long-term action item: (1) run audit to find other SAs with both permissions, (2) add automated policy check in infra provisioning pipelines, (3) add unit test to RBAC migration runner.

sanjay: note for the migration runner: default affinity rules must never contain `*` or empty label values. adding validation now.

laura: summary of immediate remediation steps taken: - deleted RoleBinding in reporting namespace - removed reporting-sa from KMS key policy - revoked reporting-sa creds/rotated keys - rolled back affinity-mapper change - exported audit of rows accessed - created P1 incident and alerted infra-sec oncall

mike: follow-ups: privacy to notify affected customers per policy if rows contained PII. security postmortem owner: laura. timeline: will draft and share within 24h.

jen: also patching onboarding scripts that created the KMS binding. adding gating to avoid granting KMS decrypt to any SA that isn't explicitly whitelist-approved.

laura: thanks team. keeping channel updated. tagging @sanjay @mike for any new alerts. :white_check_mark:
